summary: security checked in 3 executive handoff item(s)

items.summary: Security disposition: conditional for ordinary bounded reversible growth; evidence_needed for fleet-wide security assurance; blocked for SearchWoot public beta or full launch. Evidence: security baseline covers 59 sites but fleet-doctor is unavailable with no run, operations deploy/uptime/error sweeps are unavailable, and no security checks are reported. TLS has no certificates expiring within 30 days, and no active incident, credential exposure, or exploit is evidenced. Risk severity is high for go-live and security-sensitive production changes because authentication/access boundaries, secrets exposure, container isolation, release controls, dependency risk, data exposure, incident readiness, and disclosure readiness are not evidenced; medium for ordinary growth because no concrete active security incident is reported. Exact recommendation: keep SearchWoot private, queue nothing new, and continue only existing isolated reversible work with reviewer, smoke, rollback, and measurement gates. Do not claim certification or a clean bill of health from missing telemetry.

Security release decision: do not authorize SearchWoot public beta, full launch, monetization expansion, or security-sensitive production change. The launch checklist explicitly marks security_and_release blocked, while fleet-doctor and operations sweeps have no usable results. Required evidence before reconsideration: authenticated access and boundary review, secret-handling evidence, runtime/container isolation, release and rollback controls, dependency and supply-chain review, TLS and security-header evidence, data-flow and log exposure review, incident signals and response ownership, and security.txt or equivalent disclosure readiness where applicable. Missing evidence is an uncertainty, not proof of compromise.

For ordinary fleet growth, retain existing bounded reversible work only. Security does not recommend blocking routine SEO or content work solely for optional hardening when the work introduces no new data collection, credentials, access surface, deployment scope, or monetization-sensitive behavior. Existing work must remain isolated, preserve site boundaries, pass reviewer and smoke checks, document rollback, and stop on any newly observed incident, secret exposure, access-control regression, dependency concern, or data leakage signal.
